elements.description: A table of rows and columns, drawn from the same column definitions on both sides. Named `data-table` and not `table` because `<table>` is a native html element and vue refuses to redefine one. The two renderers part on what a cell value may be, and they have to: the client one runs before the data is known, so it takes functions for `format`, `href`, `icon` and `params` and resolves routes itself; the server one runs after, so it takes the result already computed in the row — `{label, href}` for a link, `{icon, href}` for an icon. `secondary` greys the header too on the client and only the body on the server, and the refreshing overlay has no server equivalent because a page that is being redrawn is not on screen.

A field extension (`extensions.expression` of any kind of field holding one value, `extension_expression.schema.json`): an expression in place of the value — a template computing it on each run. A strip under the field switches it to an editor of the given language and back; it starts as an expression when the value matches the given pattern; the value kept before is given back on the way back. The editor is the one the form hands over for code when it has one, a text area else. On a text, a number, a choice, a switch — not on pairs, tags or a colour. The same under the twig theme's field, where the editor named as the field is what the form posts.

elements.description: Pictures hung on a wall, each in a media frame, laid as the room allows.

notes.vue: its client-side twin is the entity wall (collection/wall/abstract-entity-wall)
notes.script: it shows and does nothing

elements.description: A region of a layout that folds to its bar, the bar turning on its side with it.
The handle that sizes the region it stands in, lying in the gap beside it.

A screen made of zones the reader cuts and sizes: one zone at first, split side by side or one above the other, every seam dragged, a zone held to its width or height; the arrangement a tree kept and handed back.

notes.template: client-side by nature: it only makes sense inside a vue tree
notes.script: its behaviour is the vue component's
notes.ai: cut, close and size a zone

elements.description: One node of a zone tiling: a split, drawing its children side by side or one above the other with a seam between each two, or a zone, drawing what the page puts in it.

notes.template: client-side by nature: it only makes sense inside a vue tree
notes.script: its behaviour is the vue component's
notes.ai: its actions are the tiling's

elements.description: A bar of tools on the end of a row of zones, as an IDE has one: each icon opens or closes a zone of the row, one open at a time in a group, its state kept.

notes.style: it is drawn by the toolbar and zone shapes it attaches to

shapes.description: A muted icon button for a secondary action sitting in a corner — close, expand, dismiss —, its corners the controls' own: no button of the design system is round.
An inline link with an icon beside its label, muted until hovered, for a secondary action inside text or a row.

The frames an agent draws round what it points at or presses (AgentFrameLayer, in the loader): a layer of their own over the page, so that no ancestor hiding its overflow cuts them. Each wears the assisted outline the fields wear, pulsing.  The page's layer stands under the veil an overlay draws (`--z-modal` less the veil's slot), so what was pointed at in the page dims with it; an overlay's own layer (`--inner`) stands in the overlay, at its corner, above what it holds.
A round frame at text size holding a portrait, an icon or initials, cropped to fill.
The card: a raised rectangle with a title, a body, media, meta and a footer, each optional.

A conversation one reads and writes to: the thread of its messages (shapes/thread) over the composer sending the next one (shapes/composer), and above them a bar for what concerns the conversation itself. The two parts stand alone each; this is only how they are held together.
A row of small things that wraps when it runs out of room: tags, pills, buttons.

What writes a message: a field growing with its lines, what sends it beside its last line, the files going with it above, and under it what can be done besides writing. It insets nothing: it is the field, border included, and the room around it is for whoever holds it to give.

A console: what a run writes of itself, one line per event, read as it arrives. Nothing here is for the eye — monospace, one notch down, the lines as tight as they read —, the colour alone telling the kinds apart: a state's tone on the kind, the text itself only when something went wrong. A line keeps to one line whatever it says, its end given up at the edge: the whole is read in the detail it leads to.  A line: its time, its id, the kind of event, what it concerns (a slot, a file), what it says, and what stands at the far end. Any of them may be a link or a button (`console--part`), reading as the text they are until the pointer is on them.
Centres its content and caps its width at one of the reading sizes.
Prose written elsewhere — an article, a description, rendered markdown — given spacing, headings and figures.
Icon actions in the corner of a framed thing — a code block, a lead, a block, a message —, out of the way until it is pointed at or reached by the keyboard.

What changes, field by field: what it was and what it becomes, facing each other across an arrow — the value that goes struck, the one that stays in full. Read in a sync under review, a record's history, a change to confirm.
A file or a directory shown as an icon with its name under it.
The grid that lays disk items out, wrapping at a fixed item width.
A documentation page: sections in two columns, the prose on one side and the code on the other.
What stands where a list, a table or a panel has nothing to show: said once, in the middle of the room the rows would have taken, and quietly — nothing having happened is not an error.

Files held by a field, one chip each: a thumbnail when it is an image, its kind's icon otherwise, its name — cut, whole in its title —, and the way to take it out. What a media picker shows of its choice, what a file field shows of the files dropped on it.
The default vertical rhythm between blocks, and `no-flow` to drop it where it is unwanted.
The strip closing a page, aligned on the same gutters as the rest of it.
Every form shape at once, for whoever draws a form and does not want to name them one by one.
The row closing a form, where its buttons sit.

A field with a fixed word beside its value — a unit, a currency — that is not part of it. The frame is the group's: it draws the field's border and ground, the input inside drops its own, so the word and the value sit in one field. The ring of focus goes round the whole, the frozen look too.
A field whose value is being filled for it, and how it reads while that happens.
What every input and textarea looks like before anything is said about it.
A checkbox and its label, as a row that can be clicked whole.

A field narrowing what is shown beside it — a table's rows, a menu's items, a folder's files: a magnifier and what is typed, in one frame. Written on a field with a word beside it (`form--input-group`), the magnifier being that word:
{{ icon('ph:bold/magnifying-glass') }}

A field and what acts on it, on one line: a message and its Send, a name and its Add, a search and its filter. The field takes the room, what acts on it keeps its width and never goes to another line — the shape a bar of options holds (shapes/toolbar), and a form of one question anywhere else.
The frame of a form: its groups, their labels, and how they follow one another.
The help text under a field, and the errors that replace it.
A password field and the control revealing what it holds.
A native select made to read like the other inputs, caret included.
What a field looks like when it is focused, in error, or refusing input.

A number changed one step at a time — a quantity —: a button on each side of its figure. The figure keeps the width of a few digits, centred; the browser's own spinner, too small to aim at, is left out.
Form fields set on a raised ground rather than on the page.
A checkbox drawn as a switch.
The frame a chart is drawn in, filling what it is given and clipping what overflows.
Columns that fit themselves to the room available, or a fixed number when asked.
The horizontal and vertical margins a page keeps at its edges, shared so its parts line up.
The bar at the top of a page: its title, and the controls that belong to it.
The frame of a page — a horizontal or vertical split, and a body that scrolls or does not.
The reset: box model, margins, lists and typographic defaults, applied once to the document.
An introductory paragraph, set apart in italics inside a dotted frame.
An image or a video held at a ratio — square, round, 16:9 — cropped rather than distorted.
A menu, as a bar or as a column: its items, their icons, their counts and their submenus.
A thin line of secondary information between two separators, its groups pushed to either end.
The edges of a box that can be sized: strips lying across its border, drawn nothing — the cursor is what says the edge can be pulled.

What a page does, at its foot: its actions in one row, whatever holds the page — a modal, a panel, an embed, the page's own zone. The first group stands at the start, the last one at the end: previous and next, cancel and save.
A page on its way into the room it will fill — an embed today, a modal or a panel tomorrow: the manager wears `is-page-loading`, the page it held dims, and a spinner stands in the middle of the room.

A page replaced by the next inside what holds it — a step of a tunnel in a modal: the one leaving slides a few pixels the way the visitor goes and fades, the one arriving comes in from the other side. Only a page marked `data-page-transition="slide"` moves; the classes are the page manager's.
A column with a scrolling track between fixed ends, for a side panel or a toolbar of its own.

A press answered where it landed: a wave spreading from the point touched, inside the element pressed (RippleHelper). An agent's press wears the accent, as its outline does, so the reader sees who touched.

What a thing is, said in one line: words, and its values set apart among them as markers — « reads the request, of type message, the last 10 ».  Text, not a row: the words flow and wrap word by word as a sentence does, the markers standing in the line as words do. A row (`cluster`) would wrap by pieces, a run of words falling to the next line whole; it is for things side by side, not for things said. The markers need nothing of it: they are already inline, centred on the line, the typed spaces their margin.
Children laid in a row or a column with one gap, optionally split at a point or divided by rules.

The line at the foot of what it describes — a listing, an editor, a card — saying where it stands: how many there are, which language, whether what is shown is saved. Read and never acted on: what is done to the thing is its footer's (`block--footer`), and what leads to it is a breadcrumb's.  Its height is its own, the same empty or not, so what it sits under does not jump when a word comes and goes. The part said last, at the far end, is `status-bar--end`.
The raised ground a block sits on, and the class that tells its children they are on one.

A header that sorts — a table's, a listing's — is a button dressed as the header it sits in, so the row of labels reads the same sortable or not. The arrow is always there: a faint pair while the column does not order the list, one strong arrow once it does.

The lines of a conversation read in order, the latest at the foot: a column that scrolls, the way back up to older lines at its head, what the other side is doing at its foot while it works. And the line of conversation itself — an avatar, an author and a date, the words. A line drawn from markdown is prose (`.content`), at the size of the thread.

Things one under the other, each on a marker, joined by a line: the steps of a procedure, the events of a history, the stages of a run. What each holds is free — a title, a line of text, a table, a form — and the line runs down the whole height of it, to the next marker.
A row of controls above or below what they act on, grouped and separated.
The rows of the uploads window: the design system's progress bar for each file — its name, how far it got —, and what came of it under it.

Pictures of every height packed side by side with no holes, each one at its own ratio, as a photo wall is hung. The rows are a twelfth of a column's width, so a tile is as tall as its ratio says by spanning that many twelfths: `grid-row-end: span 9` for a 4:3 landscape — what wallSpan() and the wall template work out from a width and a height. Measuring a column needs the wall to be a container, which is why the tiles sit in a box of their own: a grid cannot read its own width.
…
A region of a layout given its own size, splittable, scrollable, and never handing that size to its children.

A zone given whole to a table: the table is the region, not a sheet laid in it. Whatever drives the table — its search, its filters, its bulk actions — stands at the top, its pages at the foot, both out of what scrolls; between them the table's own ground runs to the bottom of the zone however few rows there are, and the rows scroll under a header that stays.  Any table of the system goes in it, written by the server or by a vue, with whatever holds it on the way — a collection, a mounted component: each of them, down to the table's frame, becomes a column handing its height on.
